The model war is over. The context war just started.

At Dreamforce this week, Salesforce introduced AIforce and Koa — deliberately splitting the AI interface from the trusted enterprise execution layer. Koa adds CRM-specific reasoning through a model Salesforce controls. Not OpenAI. Not Anthropic. Salesforce.

The same week, HubSpot launched Growth Context — rebuilding its CRM to continuously assemble customer context and activate it across every function. Mistral doubled down on the same thesis: enterprise AI is about control, not just intelligence.

Three major players. One converging bet. The value in enterprise AI is shifting from who has the best model to who owns the context layer — your customer data, your business logic, your workflows.

This matters for every CEO and CTO making AI architecture decisions right now. If you are plugging a general-purpose model into your stack without owning the context layer, you are building on rented ground.

GYanTech AI helps executive teams design context-first AI architectures that preserve control and strategic optionality. Link in bio.
